question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. The group of students, B. along with the professor, C. were discussing the new findings D. in the research lab.
solution_text:
The correct answer is were discussing the new findings.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The subject of the sentence is “The group of students”, and the head noun is the singular “group”.

• The phrase “along with the professor” is a parenthetical addition; it does not change the number of the subject.

• A singular subject takes a singular verb, so “were discussing” (plural) must be “was discussing” (singular).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Rule: Words/phrases joined to the subject by along with, together with, as well as, in addition to, besides do NOT affect the verb; the verb agrees with the original (main) subject.

• “Group” is a collective noun treated as singular when acting as a single unit → “The group was discussing…”.

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 2 and 4 are grammatically correct; only Part C carries the subject-verb agreement error.

question:
Identify the part of the sentence that contains a grammatical error.

A. She spoke B. so fastly that C. I could barely understand D. what she was saying.
solution_text:
The correct answer is so fastly that.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Fast” is both an adjective and an adverb; its adverb form is “fast”, not “fastly”.

• “Fastly” is not a standard English word, so “so fastly that” is incorrect.

• The correct expression is “so fast that”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Some adverbs have the same form as their adjectives (flat adverbs): fast, hard, late, early, high, low, near.

• Correct: “She spoke so fast that I could barely understand what she was saying.”

 

NOTE

• Parts A, C and D are grammatically correct; the error lies only in “so fastly that”.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate preposition:

The researchers accounted ______ all variables before finalizing the data model.
solution_text:
The correct answer is for.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrasal verb “account for” means to consider, explain, or take into account something.

• Here the researchers considered/took into account all variables, so “accounted for” is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• account for = to explain or give a reason for; also to make up a part of a total.

• Example: “We must account for every rupee spent.”

 

NOTE

• “accounted to/with/on” are not standard collocations for this meaning and are therefore incorrect.

question:
Fill in the blank with the most appropriate verb:

She ______ her position on the matter only after repeated questioning by the press.
solution_text:
The correct answer is clarified.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase “only after repeated questioning by the press” indicates a past, completed action, so a past-tense verb is required.

• “clarified” (made clear) fits the meaning – she made her position clear only after being questioned.

• “reiterates” and “deflects” are present tense and do not agree with the past-time context.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• clarify = to make something clear or easier to understand.

• reiterate = to repeat; deflect = to turn aside; assume = to take on / suppose.

 

NOTE

• “reiterates”/“deflects” are wrong tense and “deflects”/“assumes” give the wrong meaning; only “clarified” suits both grammar and sense.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Pellucid
solution_text:
The correct answer is Clear.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Pellucid” means transparently clear in style or meaning; easy to understand.

• The closest synonym among the options is “Clear”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of pellucid: clear, transparent, lucid, limpid, crystalline.

• Root: Latin ‘per-’ (through) + ‘lucere’ (to shine) → shining through.

 

NOTE

• Vague, Obscure and Ambiguous are antonyms of pellucid, so they are incorrect.

question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Querulous
solution_text:
The correct answer is Complaining.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Querulous” means complaining in a petulant or whining manner.

• The closest synonym is “Complaining”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Synonyms of querulous: complaining, peevish, petulant, grumbling, whining.

• Related root: Latin ‘queri’ = to complain.

 

NOTE

• Contented, Cheerful and Pleasant convey the opposite (positive) sense and are therefore antonyms, not synonyms.

question: Choose the correct meaning of the idiom: Out and about
solution_text:
The correct answer is Active and socializing.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The idiom “out and about” means being active and moving around, especially after an illness, or going out and mixing with people.

• Hence it best means “Active and socializing”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• out and about = able to go outside and be active again (often after being ill); busy going to places and meeting people.

• Example: “After a week in bed, she is finally out and about.”

 

NOTE

• “At home resting” is the opposite; “Doing errands” and “Traveling to distant places” are too narrow/literal and do not capture the idiom's sense.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Retired
solution_text:
The correct answer is Active.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Retired” means having withdrawn from work or active life; no longer active.

• Its antonym is “Active”, meaning engaged in work or movement.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Antonyms of retired: active, working, employed, engaged.

• Synonyms: withdrawn, inactive, resting.

 

NOTE

• Idle, Resting and Inactive are synonyms (similar in meaning) of retired, not antonyms.

question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Veracity
solution_text:
The correct answer is Falsehood.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Veracity” means truthfulness or conformity to facts.

• Its opposite is “Falsehood”, meaning the state of being untrue.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Root: Latin ‘verax/verus’ = true (cf. verify, verdict).

• Synonyms of veracity: truth, accuracy, honesty, authenticity.

 

NOTE

• Truth, Accuracy and Authenticity are synonyms of veracity, so they cannot be its antonym.

question:
Choose the correct one-word substitute for:

A style of writing characterized by exaggerated sentimentality
solution_text:
The correct answer is Melodrama.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• “Melodrama” refers to a dramatic or writing style characterized by exaggerated emotions, sensationalism and appeal to the sentiments.

• It best fits “a style of writing characterized by exaggerated sentimentality”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• melodrama = a sensational, emotionally exaggerated dramatic work; also used for over-the-top emotional behaviour.

• melodramatic (adj.) = exaggeratedly emotional.

 

NOTE

• Sentimentalism denotes a tendency to indulge in sentiment but is not the standard term for the writing style; Romanticism and Expressionism are distinct literary/art movements and do not match the definition.

question: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?
option_1: Many believed the new millennium would bring great change, but some felt embarrassed when their predictions failed.
option_2: He didn’t want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium.
option_3: The celebration of the millennium was truly unforgettable, though it did embarrass a few politicians.
option_4: She didn’t expect the event to embarrass her during the millennium gala.
solution_text:
The correct answer is He didn’t want to embarrass himself at the start of the new millenium..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word “millenium” in this sentence is misspelled; the correct spelling is “millennium” (double ‘l’ and double ‘n’).

• All the other sentences spell “millennium” and “embarrass/embarrassed” correctly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• millennium = mille (thousand) + annus (year) → two ‘l’s and two ‘n’s. Plural: millennia.

• embarrass also doubles both consonants (double ‘r’, double ‘s’).

 

NOTE

• Options 1, 3 and 4 contain no spelling errors, so they are incorrect choices.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The student said, "I have been reading this book for a month, but I still do not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part."
option_1: The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
option_2: The student said that he has been reading this book for a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.
option_3: The student said that he had been reading this book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part.
option_4: The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still does not understand the last chapter, which is the most crucial part.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The student said that he had been reading that book for a month, but he still did not understand the last chapter, which was the most crucial part..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Reporting verb “said” is in the past, so the reported speech shifts back: “have been reading” → “had been reading”, “do not understand” → “did not understand”, “is” → “was”.

• Pronoun “I” → “he” and the near demonstrative “this book” → “that book”.

• Only Option 1 applies all these changes correctly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Backshift of tenses in indirect speech: present perfect → past perfect; simple present → simple past.

• Proximals change: this → that, these → those, here → there, now → then.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 keeps present tenses/“this” (no backshift); Option 3 keeps “this book” instead of “that book”; Option 4 mixes “does not understand/is” without backshift – all incorrect.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.

The doctor said, "If you exercise regularly, you will feel better."
option_1: The doctor said that if you exercised regularly, you would feel better.
option_2: The doctor said that if he/she exercised regularly, he/she would feel better.
option_3: The doctor said that if one exercises regularly, one will feel better.
option_4: The doctor said that if one exercised regularly, one would feel better.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The doctor said that if one exercised regularly, one would feel better..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The general “you” in the direct speech refers to people in general, so it is best reported with the indefinite pronoun “one”.

• With a past reporting verb, the conditional backshifts: “exercise” → “exercised” and “will feel” → “would feel”.

• Option 4 correctly uses “one…one” with the backshifted tenses.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• In reported speech, will → would, and a first-conditional (if + present, will) becomes if + past, would.

• The generic ‘you’ is neatly replaced by ‘one’ throughout for consistency.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 keeps “you” (not fully impersonal); Option 2 introduces “he/she” wrongly; Option 3 fails to backshift (“exercises…will feel”) – hence incorrect.

question: Which sentence contains a misspelled word?
option_1: We went to a new restuarant downtown.
option_3: Is there a restaurant nearby that’s open late?
option_4: They own the oldest restaurant in town.
solution_text:
The correct answer is We went to a new restuarant downtown..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The word “restuarant” is misspelled; the correct spelling is “restaurant” (‘-au-’ before ‘r’, i.e. rest-au-rant).

• The remaining sentences spell “restaurant” correctly.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Correct spelling: r-e-s-t-a-u-r-a-n-t (from French). A common error is swapping to ‘restuarant’.

• Tip: remember “restaurant” contains the word ‘aura’ – rest-‘aura’-nt.

 

NOTE

• Options 2, 3 and 4 have no spelling mistakes, so they are not the answer.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

All the jury members was divided in their opinions.
option_1: All the jury member were divided
option_2: All the jury members were divided
option_3: All the jury were divided between their opinions
option_4: All juries have divided in their opinions
solution_text:
The correct answer is All the jury members were divided.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The plural subject “jury members” requires the plural verb “were”, not the singular “was”.

• “members” must stay plural, so “All the jury members were divided” is correct.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Subject-verb agreement: plural subject + plural verb (members were).

• ‘Divided in their opinions’ is the idiomatic collocation (not ‘between’).

 

NOTE

• Option 1 uses singular “member” with plural “were” (mismatch); Option 3 uses “between” wrongly; Option 4 changes the meaning/structure (“juries have divided”) – all incorrect.

question:
Choose the most suitable option to replace the highlighted part of the sentence:

One should do ones' duty.
solution_text:
The correct answer is One should do one's duty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The possessive form of the pronoun “one” is “one's” (with the apostrophe before ‘s’).

• The original “ones'” is wrongly placed; the correct phrase is “One should do one's duty.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• The indefinite pronoun ‘one’ takes the reflexive/possessive ‘one's’ and ‘oneself’ (formal usage), keeping consistency within the sentence.

 

NOTE

• “ones duties” and “once duties” are grammatically/lexically wrong; “their duty” breaks pronoun consistency with “one” – hence incorrect.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

You must finish your homework.
option_1: Your homework must be finished by you.
option_2: Your homework must being finished by you.
option_3: Your homework must have been finished by you.
option_4: Your homework is must be finished by you.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Your homework must be finished by you..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• With the modal “must”, the passive is formed as: modal + be + past participle.

• So “You must finish your homework” becomes “Your homework must be finished by you.”

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive with modals: subject + modal + be + V3 + by + agent.

• Example: “She can solve it” → “It can be solved by her.”

 

NOTE

• Option 2 “must being” is ungrammatical; Option 3 “must have been” changes the meaning to perfect; Option 4 “is must be” is grammatically wrong.

question:
Choose the correct passive voice transformation of the sentence:

The new intern had forgotten to lock the laboratory door before leaving.
option_1: The laboratory door was forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
option_2: The laboratory door had been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
option_3: The laboratory door has been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving.
option_4: The laboratory door had forgotten to lock by the new intern before leaving.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The laboratory door had been forgotten to be locked by the new intern before leaving..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The active sentence is in the past perfect (“had forgotten”), so the passive uses “had been + V3” → “had been forgotten”.

• The infinitive “to lock” also becomes passive “to be locked”.

• Option 2 correctly reads “had been forgotten to be locked…”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Past perfect passive: had + been + past participle.

• An object infinitive turns passive: to lock → to be locked.

 

NOTE

• Option 1 uses “was” (simple past, wrong tense); Option 3 uses “has been” (present perfect); Option 4 keeps active “to lock” – all incorrect.

question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in direct voice.

The student told his friend that he had to go home that day because he had been feeling unwell since the day before, and his parents were waiting for him.
option_1: "I have to go home today because I was feeling unwell since yesterday, and my parents are waiting for me," the student said to his friend.
option_2: "I had to go home that day because I had been feeling unwell since the day before, and my parents were waiting for me," the student said to his friend.
option_3: "I must go home today because I was feeling unwell since yesterday, and my parents were waiting for me," the student said to his friend.
option_4: "I have to go home today because I had been feeling unwell since yesterday, and my parents were waiting for me," the student said to his friend.
solution_text:
The correct answer is "I have to go home today because I was feeling unwell since yesterday, and my parents are waiting for me," the student said to his friend..

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Converting to direct speech, the backshifted tenses return to the original: “had to go” → “have to go”, “were waiting” → “are waiting”.

• Time/place words revert: “that day” → “today” and “the day before” → “yesterday”.

• The pronoun “he” → “I” and the words are placed within quotation marks. Option 1 does all this (as per the official key).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Reverse backshift in direct speech: had to → have to; were → are; that day → today; the day before → yesterday.

• Direct speech is enclosed in inverted commas with the reporting clause outside.

 

NOTE

• Option 2 keeps the backshifted forms (“had to go…that day…were waiting”); Options 3 and 4 alter modality/tense (“must”, “had been feeling”, “were waiting”) and do not restore the exact original wording, so they are treated as incorrect.

question:
India's tryst with chess is deeply interwoven with its cultural heritage, for the game itself originally known as “chaturanga” emerged on the subcontinent over a millennium ago. Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare, “chaturanga” evolved into shatranj under Persian influence before migrating westward, ultimately becoming modern chess.

 

In the contemporary era, India's prominence on the global chess stage began with the meteoric ascent of Viswanathan Anand in the late 20th century. Anand's fluid playing style, amalgamating tactical precision with positional depth, earned him the World Chess Championship title multiple times and inspired a generation of players. His success catalysed institutional investment in chess, leading to an upsurge in tournaments, academies, and grassroots initiatives across the country.

 

The 21st century has witnessed the emergence of prodigies such as Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa, D. Gukesh, and Nihal Sarin, whose exploits in international arenas have positioned India as a formidable force in team events like the Chess Olympiad. Digital platforms have further accelerated talent development, enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide, thus refining their strategic acumen from an early age.

 

Today, India stands not merely as the cradle of chess's origins but as an influential power shaping its future. This continuity from ancient invention to modern innovation underscores the nation's enduring legacy in the chess world.

 

The phrase "enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide" functions as:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Participle phrase.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase begins with the present participle “enabling” and modifies the preceding idea (Digital platforms…).

• A group of words headed by a participle that acts like an adjective is a participle (participial) phrase.

• Hence “enabling young aspirants to spar with grandmasters worldwide” is a participle phrase.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Participial phrase = participle (‑ing/‑ed) + its modifiers/objects, functioning as an adjective.

• It has no subject or finite verb, so it is not a clause.

 

NOTE

• It is not a Noun clause (it has no subject-verb clause structure), nor a mere Adverbial phrase, nor an Absolute phrase (which would have its own subject) – so those options are incorrect.

Identify the voice in "Initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare".
solution_text:
The correct answer is Passive voice.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The phrase uses the past participle “conceived” without a doer, describing something that was conceived (an action received by the subject).

• The full idea is “(chaturanga was) initially conceived as a strategic simulation of warfare” – the subject undergoes the action, which is the mark of the passive voice.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• Passive voice: subject receives the action; formed with be + past participle (was conceived).

• Reduced/elliptical passives often drop ‘be’, leaving just the past participle (conceived).

 

NOTE

• Active voice would need the subject doing the action; “Middle” and “Causative” voices do not apply to this construction, so they are incorrect.

question:
Which of the following pairs of homonyms can be used to fill in the blanks most suitably?

The interior designer received a ______ from her client for choosing furniture that would perfectly ______ the walls and floors.
solution_text:
The correct answer is compliment, complement.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The first blank needs a noun meaning praise → “compliment” (the designer received praise from the client).

• The second blank needs a verb meaning to go well with / match → “complement” (furniture that would complement the walls and floors).

• Hence the correct pair is “compliment, complement”.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information (Exam-oriented)

• compliment = praise/admiration (noun/verb).

• complement = something that completes or goes well with another (noun/verb).

• Tip: complement ‘completes’ – both have the letter ‘e’ after ‘compl’.

 

NOTE

• “counsel/council” (advice / an assembly) do not fit the meaning; “complement, compliment” reverses the required order, so those options are incorrect.
